::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 29th 1877  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)

Thank you for your pretty card of arum lilies, I suppose they are decking the Church with them in the southern hemisphere I am ashamed not to send you one – a card I mean not a lily, but I got fewer than usual this year and have pretty much disposed of them - I suppose your decorations were made agreeable this year by the splendid crop of holly berries We have had a very pleasant evening – or rather night of private theatricals at Hursley Park. They had Goldsmith’s real play of [the Goodnatured man](other_books/otherbook_898.qmd), and it went off with great spirit the Heathcotes and Wilsons all act so well[^1] The last thing was a charming little piece bringing out the likeness of the twins – who conspire (as Breton peasant girls) to ?tire down a fisher man who thinks both are one. That little Albrook schoolmistress goes on well, but she goes home to Southampton every Saturday. I don’t know anything about [Mr Sloggett](people/person_2314.qmd)’s womenkind but I like himself he is [SPG](organizations/other_41.qmd) secretary and has been an Indian chaplain, Low Church but just like a picture of a clergyman in the good little books of 20 years ago. I don’t know much about Hyde[^2] I hope to fit [Fernando](other_books/otherbook_741.qmd) all into this volume That book of [Mrs Charles Martin](people/person_968.qmd)s [‘An Old looking glass’](other_books/otherbook_899.qmd) is perfectly admirable for servants. Seely publishes it.[^3]

with New Year’s wishes to you and Cherry[^4]
your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: The actors were the children of [Sir William Heathcote](people/person_669.qmd) and the [Rev. R. F. Wilson](people/person_1541.qmd).
[^3]: The Rev. Charles Sloggett was Vicar of St. Bartholomew, Hyde, Winchester. He had a wife and five children.
[^4]: Maria Louisa Charlesworth, *The Old Looking-Glass, or, Mrs Dorothy Cope’s Recollections of Service* (London Seeley 1878 [1877]).  Perhaps it had been recommended by Dora Frances Moberly (1841-1926) who had married the Rev. Charles Martin (1840-1910) in 1869.
[^5]: 'Cherry' seems to have been the novel Coleridge was working on, subsequently published as *An English Squire*
